rows.description: A toddler beckons with a curled hand to call a parent or pushes a hand outward to refuse or send something away. These early gestures carry wanting, protest or invitation, and meaning depends on what the child is looking at.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler learns that a caregiver's raised palm paired with a firm voice means stop, mostly from tone and context. The gesture alone is a cue to pause, not proof of anger; a calm face usually means safety, not scolding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, calm, trust

rows.description: A toddler stretches arms wide for big, cups hands to show a bowl, or reaches toward a wanted object. These gestures often come before words and show desire, comparison or pride; adults who name the meaning aloud help language grow.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler follows an adult's point toward a dog or toy and starts pointing to share interest. The gesture signals look at this, I want that or what is that; caregivers gain from checking what the child actually looks at before guessing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Body tension and slump as signals [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler stiffens with anger, goes limp in a tantrum or leans against a parent when tired. These are mostly body states rather than planned messages; a calm adult reads them as need for rest, comfort or help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, tiredness, calm

rows.description: A toddler notices whether a parent is crouched down and relaxed or standing stiff. A lowered, open posture usually feels safe, while looming and tense feels threatening; young children react to the body long before understanding the words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler bounces with delight, stamps feet in frustration or runs in circles from excitement. Whole-body motion often shows feeling before language does; naming it, for instance you are so happy, builds emotional words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, anger, excitement

rows.description: A toddler rocks, sways or bounces on a knee to calm down or fall asleep. It is a common way to settle strong feelings; persistent or distressing rocking with poor contact is worth mentioning to a paediatrician.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler buries the face in a parent's shoulder or hides behind legs when meeting strangers. It signals shyness or fear rather than rudeness; letting the child warm up at their own pace supports trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, fear, shyness, trust

rows.description: A toddler flinches, jerks arms out or freezes at a loud noise or a sudden movement. These are reflexive protective responses, not misbehaviour; a soothing voice and a hold help the body settle.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
